actions.mechanism: Customer round-robin prevents bulk submissions from monopolizing dispatches; FIFO within each customer prevents job starvation.
actions.implementation: Keep one ready-list entry per customer. Dispatch its oldest job, then reappend if backlogged. Append newly active customers at the tail.
actions.check: With N customers ahead, dispatch occurs within 60(N+1) seconds. Test continuous heavy arrivals and occasional shorts with 4× estimate errors; measure mean latency separately.
actions.risk: This bounds dispatch waiting, not equal compute consumption; bounds grow with customer count.

actions.action: Offer short jobs three of four customer turns.
actions.mechanism: Estimated-shortest selection improves short-job opportunities; mandatory oldest-job turns protect underestimated priority and long-job progress.
actions.implementation: Within customer round-robin, count dispatches per customer. Choose estimated-shortest for three turns, then oldest for the fourth; reset the counter.
actions.check: Under continuous heavy arrivals and reversed runtime rankings, verify every fourth customer dispatch selects oldest. Compare short-job latency against FIFO without assuming improvement.
actions.risk: Nonpreemption still permits sixty-second blocking; inaccurate estimates can erase latency benefits.

actions.action: Alternatively, reserve two workers for guaranteed progress.
actions.mechanism: A protected customer rotation guarantees service while ten workers pursue estimated-shortest jobs across customers.
actions.implementation: Assign two existing workers to customer round-robin with FIFO selection; assign ten to estimated-shortest. Atomically remove selected jobs from shared queues.
actions.check: On the protected rotation, N customers ahead imply dispatch within 60(N+1) seconds. Test continuous heavy arrivals and inverted estimates; report maximum customer wait separately from mean latency.
actions.risk: Protected workers can be occupied for sixty seconds; global shortest selection may favor inaccurate estimates.
